operations.value:
No native tooltip reliably appears in the desktop app's sidebar on macOS (Electron 44.2.0): rail project tiles, the rail category fold button and the expanded sidebar's category header show nothing on hover, while tooltips elsewhere in the window work.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by Dylan's hover A/B on 2026-10-16): upstream Electron/Chromium bug electron/electron#49843 (macOS, Electron 38+, Chromium 140 roll). When the pointer moves between different nodes inside one titled element (row padding -> dot -> key text -> name text), Chromium clears and re-sets the same tooltip, which macOS's tooltip manager treats as exit+enter, so the tooltip shows on the first hover and rarely after. The window structure (BaseWindow, WebContentsViews, hiddenInset, parked board views), drag regions, redraws and keyboard focus were all ruled out. A repeated-hover test with five draggable Workbench-shaped tiles: as built today, unreliable; with the tile's children set to pointer-events: none, reliable; with a full-size ::after overlay on the tile, reliable.

DECIDED WITH DYLAN: CSS hit-test workaround that keeps native tooltips (not a renderer-drawn tooltip). Accepted consequence: double-click-to-rename moves from the category name to the whole category header, so the name can stop taking the pointer.

Acceptance: hovering rail tiles, rail category buttons, the expanded sidebar's category header and the version line shows the tooltip reliably on repeated hovers on macOS; clicking, dragging, renaming (double-click on the header), keyboard focus and screen-reader names keep working; a guard keeps new titled sidebar elements from regressing.
